supply_question.question: Can NAICS 541519 alone sustain a WEEKLY brief cadence?
supply_question.verdict: NO — not with a 10+ day response window as a quality bar. A second NAICS is required.
supply_question.dedup_note: The 4 qualifying notices in the 45-day window are only 3 DISTINCT solicitations: 19AQMM26R0250 (CODIS Phase III) appears twice as a Presolicitation and a Solicitation. Counting notices instead of solicitations overstates supply by a third here.
supply_question.why_widening_the_window_does_not_help: Going from 7 to 45 days of POSTING history took the qualifying pool from 2 notices to 4 and the distinct-solicitation pool to 3. It cannot do better: a wider posting window mostly adds notices whose deadlines have ALREADY PASSED. 71 of the 119 notices in the 45-day pull (60%) were expired at run time. The binding constraint is the arrival rate of new set-aside notices, not how far back we look.

flow_rate_the_number_that_matters.interpretation: About 9 small-business set-aside solicitations per week are posted in 541519, but only about 2.8 per week ever give a bidder 10 or more days to respond. Roughly two thirds of federal small-business notices in this niche are effectively closed to anyone who is not already watching daily. 2.8 briefable items per week across the WHOLE niche means an individual subscriber -- who matches only a subset by state, certification and capability -- can expect weeks with zero matches.

supply_question.consequence_for_the_product: A weekly cadence promised on 541519 alone will miss weeks. Options, in order of cost: (1) add a second NAICS -- 541512 or 541513 -- and sell the pair as one subscription; (2) drop the 10-day bar to 7 days, which roughly doubles supply but ships briefs on notices a small firm realistically cannot answer; (3) sell a fortnightly cadence and stop promising weekly. Option 1 is the only one that does not degrade the product. This is a FOUNDER decision, not an agent decision.

set_aside_field_states.note: counts over the 21-day pull; blank is NOT 'no set-aside'

prospect_filter.contract: Nothing is silently dropped. Every input firm appears in exactly one of kept/excluded, and every exclusion records the rule, the literal token that matched and the evidence text it matched in. Selftest asserts this.
prospect_filter.most_important_finding: A dollar-based size test CANNOT catch the self-certified giants, and the run instruction's premise that it could is wrong. In this scan CARAHSOFT appears at $4,500 total and SHI INTERNATIONAL at $15,331, because the scan only sees their 541519 self-certified-small awards over 24 months -- a sliver of their real business. Any ceiling low enough to catch them would delete most of the genuine small firms. That is why R2 (curated name list) exists as an INDEPENDENT rule, and the selftest pins the CARAHSOFT case specifically so a later edit cannot quietly delete the name list as redundant.
measurement_limits_recorded_in_the_outpu: total_amount is one-NAICS, one-window, page-capped -- it UNDERSTATES every firm, so the ceiling test is ONE-SIDED: over the line is decisive, under it proves nothing.
USAspending small_business is per-award self-certification, not a size determination.
latest_award is a period-of-performance START date; renamed latest_award_pop_start in the filtered output and flagged when it is in the future. Never an award date.
Industry classification reads contracting-officer free text; some says nothing.
prospect_filter.bug_found_and_fixed_during_the_run: The first version matched markers as bare substrings, so 'TENT' fired inside 'CONTENT' and excluded SOFTWARE INFORMATION RESOURCE CORP -- an Atlassian/Salesforce licensing firm, and one of the strongest prospects in the list. Markers now match on a LEADING word boundary, which still catches plurals and suffixes. That firm is now kept and ranks 2nd by fitness.
prospect_filter.resellers_kept_deliberately: Most of the top-ranked kept firms are hardware/software resellers (FCN-type VARs). They are NOT excluded: small resellers genuinely bid small-business set-asides and are plausible buyers. They carry a RESELLER_SIGNAL flag so the founder can decide commercially. This is the honest character of 541519's small-business awardee pool, and it should inform how the product is pitched.

outreach.status: 20 DRAFTS PREPARED, NOTHING SENT. No email address was known and none was invented.
outreach.why_only_7_opportunities: That is the entire currently-open, 10+ day pool in 541519 after removing a sole-source notice (142082-26-0440, GRAW Software Support -- not competable, must not be pitched) and a presolicitation whose deadline is 339 days out (1301381741, XACTA software). Several firms therefore share an opportunity. That is unavoidable at this supply and is disclosed in the batch log.
outreach.contact_lookup: The `to:` line of every draft is [EMAIL — look up on sam.gov entity search]. The batch log carries the exact SAM.gov entity-search procedure and, per firm, the legal name and the USAspending award ID to use as the lookup key. UEIs were NOT available: normalize_award() does not collect recipient UEI, so the award ID is the key -- the founder reads the UEI off the USAspending award page, then searches it on SAM.gov.
compliance_checks_enforced_programmatica: No URLs in any draft (generator asserts on http://, https://, www.) -- federal records are cited by solicitation number, SAM notice ID and USAspending award ID instead.
No attachments; the sample brief is inline plain text.
CAN-SPAM block with [POSTAL_ADDRESS] placeholder and the verbatim unsubscribe line.
Reply-to-inbox call to action; no website reference, no click.
Truthful subject naming the solicitation and the firm.
AI-assistance disclosure once in the message and once in the brief footer.
Body word count 130-145 against the skill's 110-160 limit.
Zero banned-list tokens (vetted/qualif*/winnable/guarantee/probability/strong chance) across all 20 briefs and all 20 drafts.
outreach.suppression: state/suppression.json read before drafting; it is empty, so no firm was skipped. Because no addresses are known yet the check ran against FIRM NAMES. It MUST be re-run against the real email addresses once looked up, before sending. This is stated at the top of the batch log.

qc.performed_by: a separate subagent per .claude/skills/brief-qc/SKILL.md; the writer did not QC its own work
qc.scope: the 20 briefs whose packets carry generated_utc 2026-08-30
qc.batch_specific_check: Award-ID/URL integrity: for every 'Why you're seeing this' line, the award ID in the sentence was compared against the CONT_AWD_<id> segment of the accompanying USAspending URL and against the packet's match.reasons. All 20 match character-for-character. This was the highest-risk failure mode in the batch -- pairing a firm's name with another firm's award -- and it is clean.
qc.qc_self_test: The QC agent seeded seven defects into a copy of one brief (wrong median, orphan dollar figure, altered URL, award-ID/URL mismatch, incumbent-as-fact, banned outcome words, deleted AI disclosure, wrong day count) and confirmed its script caught all of them, then hand-read five briefs in full.
qc.action_taken_on_a_non_blocking_note: QC noted the phrase 'whether your record qualifies' in two briefs -- judged PASS because it asks about the solicitation's past-performance criterion rather than offering a verdict, but it uses a word CLAUDE.md bans. It was reworded to 'which of your past projects you can actually cite', the two briefs and their drafts were regenerated, and the SAME independent QC agent re-verified them so the PASS applies to the artifacts actually on disk.
qc.open_structural_finding_from_qc: Two recurring sentence types are TRUE and were verified by QC against state/prospect_scan-541519.json and state/opportunities.json, but are NOT derivable from the packet alone: 'Your cited award is ...' (19 of 20 briefs) and 'also appears as a separate Presolicitation notice' (8 of 20). A packet-only QC pass cannot confirm them. RECOMMENDED NEXT CHANGE: have build_sample_packet copy the cited award's description and a duplicate_notices field into the packet, so every claim in a brief is packet-derivable. Not done this run -- it changes the packet schema and was outside the run's scope.
qc.expected_grep_hit: The word 'incumbent' appears in the 7 CODIS briefs only as the compliant negation 'This notice record does not name an incumbent'. That is the required framing, not a violation.

data_quality_observations: SUPPLY, the headline: widening the SAM posting window from 7 to 21 to 45 days moved the usable pool from 2 to 4 to 4 notices -- and those 4 are only 3 DISTINCT solicitations. 60% of the 45-day pull (71 of 119) was already expired at run time. Widening the window adds history, not supply.

FLOW RATE is the number to plan on: ~9 distinct small-business set-aside solicitations per week are posted in 541519, but only ~2.8 per week ever carry a 10+ day response window. Roughly two thirds of SB notices in this niche give under 10 days.

De-duplication is still not implemented. 3 solicitations in the 45-day pull appear twice each (Presolicitation + Solicitation): 36C25226R0071, 36C24626Q0522, 19AQMM26R0250. Counting notices instead of solicitations overstates the biddable pool by a third. The briefs disclose the duplicate where it occurs, but the pipeline should collapse them.
25 of 101 notices in the 21-day pull have a BLANK set_aside field, distinct from the 23 that say NONE. Blank is not full-and-open. Every brief built on a blank field says so explicitly.

One notice in the open pool is sole-source (142082-26-0440, 'SOLE SOURCE: GRAW Software Support') and one presolicitation has a deadline 339 days out (1301381741, XACTA software). Both were excluded from outreach by hand. The pipeline has no filter for either -- a future run could pitch a sole-source notice unless one is added.

The USAspending small_business flag is per-award self-certification. The new filter's R2 name rule -- NOT the dollar ceiling -- is what catches CARAHSOFT ($4,500 in this scan) and SHI INTERNATIONAL ($15,331). A dollar test alone is structurally incapable of it.

candidate_related finally produced hits: 3 awards on the FDIC/Copado notice, the first non-empty result this feature has returned on real data. They are weak matches -- the title-overlap heuristic fired on the generic words 'software', 'subscription', 'renewal', and one of the three surfaced awards belongs to another firm in this same batch. The briefs label it a heuristic and tell the reader to verify, per the skill, but the feature is not yet earning its place.

prospects: 'latest_award' remains the period-of-performance START date, not the award date. The filtered output renames it latest_award_pop_start and flags future values. It is used nowhere in any brief or draft. The underlying field in sb_award_scan is still mislabeled and still NOT fixed.
The award scan is page-capped at 500 rows (scan_capped=true), so the 121-firm prospect list is a floor, not a census, and every total_amount understates the firm.
